title: Secondary Break Trailer Three
description: After the initial fast break settles, a trailing big sprints in for a kick-out three-pointer — the 'secondary break' shot many teams rely on.

content.objective: Deliver and finish the kick-out three-pointer created by a trailing player after the initial break.
content.setup: A primary break group of two or three pushes ahead while a trailing shooter sprints a step behind.
instructions: The initial break attacks the rim, drawing defensive attention.
The trailer sprints in and spots up beyond the arc, already squared to shoot.
The ball handler kicks the ball out to the trailer rather than forcing a tough shot.
The trailer catches and shoots immediately, no hesitation.
coachingPoints: The trailer must sprint, not jog, to arrive in time.
Kick the ball out early rather than forcing a contested finish.
Trailer should be squared up and ready before the ball arrives.
commonMistakes: Trailer arriving too late because they jogged instead of sprinting.
Ball handler forcing a tough shot instead of trusting the trailer.
Jogging back instead of sprinting to get into position.
content.safety: Make sure the trailer's sprint lane is clear of defenders retreating.
